method: Complete static parsing of shortcut structures and Python execution paths; atomscan and cleave facts before edits; atomscan after edits. No specimen network or shell commands were executed. Actual Python function definitions were exercised with mock TLS, HTTP, files, chmod, subprocess and time APIs.

evidence: ZIP contains exactly launch.lnk (404 bytes) and stage.txt (11 bytes). Both member bytes match the existing first-reasoned-review regression generator.
LNK flags 0xa0 contain only HasArguments and IsUnicode. No target ID list, LinkInfo, relative path or environment target exists; StringData is followed only by a zero terminal block.
Arguments request headless conhost with cmd /c, extraction of settings.ini from TEMP/inner.zip, copying it to TEMP/runner.bat, and invoking that batch, with && success gates and output redirection.
No inner.zip or extracted configuration is supplied or acquired. The only stage content is @echo off CRLF and is not referenced by the shortcut.
There is no implemented theft, spying, destructive action, backdoor, network acquisition or persistence in the supplied artifact.
judgments.missing_context: No surrounding machine state or separately supplied external archive is available. Those are not assumed.
judgments.marker: LNK test archive: targetless fixture, no payload; remove hostile rule

judgments.identification: Sanitized targetless PowerShell output shortcut fixture
evidence: The 214-byte LNK is byte-identical to the regression builder for temp-references.lnk. It has only argument and Unicode flags and no executable target.
Decoded UTF-16LE arguments are /c powershell -nop -c Write-Output "%TEMP%\one.txt %TEMP%\two.txt".
Even if passed to cmd, this prints the expanded path text. It does not read, write, copy, download or execute those files.

The previous data-extension objective mistook a filename reference for dropper behavior. The remaining Signature Base suspicious finding is its broad -nop convenience-flag heuristic, not evidence of a payload.
judgments.missing_context: No malicious payload or deployment is supplied; hidden-window and NoProfile options alone do not establish hostile intent.
judgments.marker: LNK output fixture: prints TEMP filenames; fix data-argument trait

evidence: main requires an operator targets file or vulnerable-target list. No arguments cause no scan; --vuln only reads and displays entries.
For --targets, obtains each server TLS certificate, parses X.509, extracts its public key, encrypts username;;Windows;;timestamp;0.0.0.0 using RSA PKCS1v15 padding, and Base64-encodes the result.

POSTs a caller-derived GlobalProtect login URL with user, empty passwd and forged portal-userauthcookie, disabling TLS verification. Only status 200 with <jnlp> returns a cookie; this does not prove real-world exploit success.

On a positive result, writes a cookie and Bash helper to temporary files. The helper pipes the supplied operator sudo password and cookie to sudo -S openconnect with GlobalProtect options and background mode, then removes the cookie file. Python chmods the helper to 0700 and launches it with /bin/bash.

The helper retains the operator password in a local temporary script and interpolates CLI/target text without robust quoting. These are implementation hazards, without evidence of intentional credential theft or deception.
No hidden callback, credential harvesting, persistence, destructive action or secondary payload is present. Explicit exploit functionality is consistent with the declared scanner/connection purpose.
The real authentication-bypass capability warrants one suspicious objective. No evidence establishes that this sample was deployed against unauthorized targets.

external_context.finding: Vendor confirms GlobalProtect authentication bypass when authentication override cookies and a specific certificate configuration are used. This corroborates the mechanism, not this sample provenance or operator authorization.

judgments.missing_context: Author provenance, target ownership, testing authorization, affected gateway configuration and actual VPN connection success are unknown.
judgments.marker: GlobalProtect PoC: explicit operator tool; retain one bypass warning

trait_changes.lnk: Retired argument-only hostile conhost/batch rule. Existing neutral headless/extract/copy/batch observations remain. Removed duplicate batch argument matcher and redirected its consumer to the canonical argument/file trait.
trait_changes.data_arguments: Moved data-filename reference out of dropper objectives to process/argument/file at notable severity; updated both consumers. Naming and scope now assert a filename argument, not execution or file access.
trait_changes.vpn: Retired credential-access cookie-forgery and VPN-tunnel hostile composites. Added a single suspicious exploit-attempt composite requiring cookie-format, login endpoint, HTTP POST, TLS certificate retrieval, encryption, RSA padding and Base64 operation evidence. Session format by itself is notable.
trait_changes.crypto: Moved algorithm-unspecified Python encrypt call from symmetric/encrypt to crypto/encrypt and removed inherited obfuscation and Encrypt Data mappings. Added structured TLS-certificate retrieval, PEM parsing and RSA padding observations.
trait_changes.shell: Moved explicit Bash argv launch from subprocess to shell/interpreter, corrected its mapping to T1059.004, and updated exact consumers.
trait_changes.ancestor_consumers: Audited subtree references. A source-scoped Python-encrypt-or-symmetric group preserves the ransomware source consumer original accepted alternatives. It excludes binary types so broad binary crypto-count consumers gain no derived group. Subprocess ancestor consumers retain run/Popen/call observations for the moved Bash invocation; process/create ancestors retain membership. Exact consumers were updated, including metadata profiles.
trait_changes.exceptions: No sample basename, hash, dependent-package or arbitrary identity exclusion was added.

verification.integrity: All three original SHA-256 values verified; both shortcut structures independently reconstructed byte-for-byte.
verification.shortcut_controls: 26 existing regression controls passed, including targetless and real-target variants, absent operations, different source/sink names, icons, window settings, startup operations and inventory.
verification.vpn_controls: Seven positive/negative source controls passed: complete attempt, missing POST, missing encryption, ordinary cookie format, quoted source only, Bash argv, and encryption comments. Actual PoC paths also passed with side effects mocked.
verification.rule_trace: Six revised/new traits verified by full-ID cleave test-rules; the suspicious exploit composite matched all eight required legs.
verification.final_rescans: atomscan --no-update --follow=none --format json on each original path; 0 hostile and at most 1 suspicious per sample.
verification.analysis_limits: Atomscan reports incomplete source flow provenance. Conclusions use direct source review and controlled mocked execution as well as extracted facts. Live exploitation and VPN success were not tested.
